title: Store-local consent records are forgeable or replayable across preseeded or copied scopes

attack_path_facts.title: Store-local consent records are forgeable or replayable across preseeded or copied scopes
attack_steps: A lower-trust archive contributor supplies a copied or preseeded .kcs store containing a self-consistent scope_id plus forged persistent network and, optionally, send_secrets approval rows.
The victim adopts the store; repository open validates schema and ULID shape but not consent provenance or current-root binding.
The victim later invokes an online-capable index, resume, retry, or search workflow with a configured provider.
KCS trusts the supplied approvals, skips fresh network consent and secret holds for the matching tool, and sends eligible local content through the victim's configured adapter.
assumptions: The victim adopts a lower-trust copied or preseeded store rather than an already private live store being arbitrarily modified.
A matching provider and credential are configured and the victim invokes an eligible online command.
Offline mode and network revocation are not active.
attack_path_facts.context: The source actor is the threat model's explicit untrusted shared/archive-state contributor. The forged row does not choose a new destination, but it turns attacker-supplied state into victim network and secret-release authority without proving that the current operator granted it.
attack_path_facts.in_scope: yes; copied/preseeded store adoption and current scope-by-adapter consent authenticity are explicit I1/I3 boundaries
attack_path_facts.exposure: filesystem-supplied persisted state followed by an operator-invoked outbound adapter call; no public listener
attack_path_facts.identity: the untrusted store contributor controls scope metadata and approval rows; KCS later uses the victim OS identity and configured provider credential
attack_path_facts.cross_boundary: yes; untrusted archive state crosses into network-authorization and secret-release decisions, then can cause local content to cross the external-adapter boundary
attack_path_facts.preconditions: plausible but multi-step: victim adopts supplied state, has online adapter configuration, invokes an eligible command, and has not revoked network use
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes; the supplied-store contributor controls the self-matching scope_id and unsigned approval records consumed by the gates
attack_path_facts.category: forged/replayed persistent authorization and consent provenance failure
mitigations: Offline mode and network revocation override stored consent.
Approval remains scoped to a known adapter tool_id and execution mode.
The victim must adopt the store and invoke an online-capable command.
Documentation treats .kcs as portable authoritative state, creating ambiguity for trusted moves but not authenticating an untrusted import.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: internal-only; adopted local store plus later operator command, with no authentication of the stored consent's author
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: network authorization, secret-release policy, and confidentiality of content in one adopted scope
attack_path_facts.target_reach: one adopted scope and each matching configured adapter; send_secrets rows can affect secret-classified chunks in that scope
secrets_references: Victim provider credentials are attached to the later request.
A forged approval_method=send_secrets row can release secret-classified content to the configured provider.
counterevidence: A row copied from a different scope_id is rejected.
The destination remains the victim's configured provider rather than an attacker-selected endpoint in this candidate.
Offline mode, revocation, absent credentials, or no later eligible command defeats the send.
blindspots: No same-ID forged-store end-to-end send was retained.
The evidence does not establish that the archive contributor also controls or can observe the configured provider destination.
attack_path_facts.rationale: The preseeded-store contributor is a realistic lower-trust actor expressly included by the threat model, so same-user and operator-only suppression do not apply. Forged approval can release secret-bearing data, but adoption and a later configured online workflow constrain likelihood; high impact plus medium likelihood maps to medium.
